Worlds and world coins (Opus run) — semantic diff

Branch feature/worlds-and-world-coins-opusBase 2cf090eHead 1a122bb Target mainDate 2026-11-16 Commits 8Files 43 · +2642 / −127 Written by REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

Players choose one of 13 worlds in three sizes before Play, Training or a room's start. Three worlds are free in Small; the others and bigger sizes cost world coins, earned per 500 trophies or from ten hack codes usable once every 30 days per account.

  • New game data: worlds.ts (catalogue, sizes, seeded maps) and worldShop.ts (earning, buying, growing), all tested for every world and size.
  • Saved progress v8 with five world fields; older saves migrate and get world coins for trophies they already had; two tabs merge without undoing a reset.
  • Rooms send the host's world; friends on the previous version are removed outside Canyon Small and told to update.
  • Thirteen themes drawn from simple shapes; a Large world ran at 60 fps at iPad size in the browser.
  • World-coin codes are checked by the server; the 30-day dates live in each account on the device.

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups — every statement is met and tested; four non-blocking findings have targets.

Spec context

2026_11_16_worlds_and_world_coins_opus_spec.md — statements S1–S24; Steps 1–8 (all done).

Semantic diff

Why: Every match and Training session was played in the same arena, the same size. Players asked for several worlds in a small, medium and large size; free worlds come in Small, other worlds and bigger sizes are unlocked with world coins, earned per 500 trophies or from hack codes each account can use once every 30 days.

Breaking: Saves move to version 8 (older game versions cannot read them). In rooms, friends on the previous version can only play in Canyon Small; in another world they are removed and told to update. · Checks: 7 pass · 2 n/a · 0 fail

Author Q&A

Why generated maps instead of hand-made ones?
39 maps would be slow to write and review (D3). Each world and size has a fixed seed; a seed whose map shuts a spawn, the start or a dummy away from the centre is skipped, and the tests check every map.
Can a world-coin code be used early?
Only by clearing the browser's data: the dates live in the account on the device (D10). Server-side tracking is a deferred item.
Why does a reset in one tab not come back from the other tab's larger values?
The "larger value" merge (sizes, steps, code dates) applies only when both tabs changed the field; when only this tab changed it, its value wins.

What changed: On a start whose world is not Canyon Small, members without version get update-the-game, leave the seats, and the host gets removed and a left per slot. Why it matters: An older game cannot build another world; without this it would play a different match than the host. Check: The removed friend keeps its socket but its input is dropped (seat in room.seats); the host's HostMatch hands the empty fighter to a bot.

240 arena = generate(seed + attempt * 7919, width, depth)
241 if (arena.walls.length + arena.bushes.length === cover && playable(arena)) break
242 }
243 }
244 cache.set(key, arena)
245 return arena

What changed: Canyon Small is CANYON; other maps come from a seed and are cached; a seed whose map shuts a point in is skipped. Why it matters: Fixed maps per world and size without 39 hand-made layouts (D3). Check: The loop has no upper bound; the tests cover all 39 maps (finding 4).

Good: rules are plain functions with tests for every world and size; old saves and older room clients were thought through; the Step notes explain each deviation from the plan.

Not covered

  • Text-only changes of the five dictionaries (ui/src/lib/i18n/*.ts): 30 keys each; i18n.test.ts checks they are complete.
  • Styles of WorldScreen.svelte, Home.svelte, Arena.svelte, FriendsScreen.svelte: layout only.
  • The result screen's "+250 world coins" line: needs a finished match that crosses a 500-step; covered by earnWorldCoins tests.
  • The Hack screen's list of used codes and the QR page: checked in the browser in Step 7; their data comes from useWorldCode and /api/hacks (cards above).
  • Tests, README, docs/architecture.md and the spec: read, not shown as hunks.

Concepts glossary

async def
A coroutine: it runs on the event loop and awaits each send, so messages leave in order.
Slicing
Skips slot 0 (the host); the host is always of the current version.
isinstance
Checks the JSON value is a dict before reading keys from it; room messages come from untrusted clients.
Module constant
Canyon Small, defined once; compared with == against the incoming dict, so key order does not matter.
Optional field
A Pydantic field with a default; it is in every response, null for normal hacks, so old clients ignore it.
Unpacking a generator
Spreads one Hack per world code into the list literal, so the codes are not repeated by hand.
Single source of numbers
The 250 per step comes from SETTINGS, so changing the price in one place also changes the migration.
as const
Narrows the literal to the exact types 'canyon' / 'small', so it fits WorldId and WorldSize.
Object spread
Copies the v7 fields, then adds the five world fields on top; later keys win.
Derived value
The steps already reached are computed from the total trophies, so the migration pays them exactly once.
Clamp
Keeps the merged balance from going below 0 when both tabs spent world coins.
Three-way merge
Compares base (last synced), local and remote: a value only this tab changed is taken as is; when both changed, the larger one wins.
Ordered sizes
Sizes compare by their place in the small, medium, large tuple.
Discriminated union
The ok field tells TypeScript which shape follows, so callers must handle the refusal before reading progress.
Memoisation
Each world and size is generated once per page; Arena and the gallery reuse the same object.
Retry loop
Tries the next seed until the map is playable and has all its cover; deterministic, so the same map every time.
Default parameter
needSight defaults to true; false here picks the nearest opponent even out of sight.
Named constant
The 6 seconds of D5 in one exported place; the tests use it too.
Type guard
isWorldCode narrows Hack so world_coins and reuse_days are numbers in useWorldCode.
Milliseconds
Date.now() counts milliseconds, so the reuse days become milliseconds before they are added.
Optional property
Hosts of the previous version send no world; the type says so and sharedWorld handles it.
Runtime validation
TypeScript types vanish at run time; the value from the network is checked before it is used as a WorldId.
